### problem_chain
Root: the customer wants "the guarantee settled and the money that is owed under it paid out to Cedarhurst now" → `energy_ext_shortfall_settlement` (subject `energy_shortfall_paid`, tool `pay_savings_shortfall_2f1bc21a`, owner=agent). A `shortfall_claim` request (row `3c9805c6`, outcome received, 2026-09-16) stands, matching the blueprint's "the customer alone … lodges the claim on a guarantee".

Hop 1. Its rule's prerequisite sentence: "The shortfall paid against the guarantee is worked out only after a signed-off verification of the measured savings for the true-up period stands on the subscription's record." At the opening the only `energy_savings_verified` row is `319405cb` for billing_period 2025 (verified 2025-11-20); the current true-up period (subscription year 2025-10-01 → 2026-09-30, carried on the ledger as period "2026": `energy_guarantee_credited` row `7428c576` and `energy_analyst_hours_credited` row `b11c9017` both carry billing_period 2026) has no verification → unmet. The one write that brings that state about: `energy_ext_savings_verification` / `verify_period_savings_a6d7fa6e` (the only tool creating an `energy_savings_verified` row).

Hop 2. The verification rule's prerequisite sentence: "The savings verified for a true-up period are worked out only after the baseline standing on the subscription has been restated from the close of the replacement or retrofit project at the building." At the opening `last_change_type=users_added` (2026-04-14), `baseline_kwh=6480000` is the 2021-10 → 2023-09 baseline stated at onboarding; a project at the site closed 2026-03-20 (`retrofit_projects.895ad441`, status closed) after the last baseline statement → unmet. The one write: `energy_ext_retrofit_baseline_reset` / `reset_performance_baseline_0e66b991` (the only tool that writes `baseline_kwh` and stamps `baseline_reset`).

Hop 3. The reset rule's prerequisite sentence: "The reset baseline is fixed only once the metered points the subscription covers match the points the site meters." At the opening `meters_covered=30`; the metered points that posted a reading in the month ending NOW are 34 distinct `meter_ref`s (34 interval-meter rows, all posted 2026-09-05) → 30 ≠ 34, unmet. The one write: `energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment` / `authorise_meter_coverage_01d41e30` (the only tool writing `meters_covered`). Its rule carries no prerequisite sentence; the walk stops.

Tree derived: amendment →(state_gate: meters_covered)→ reset →(value_input: baseline_kwh feeds `baseline_use`)→ verification →(value_input: the verified/guaranteed figures feed `guaranteed_latest`/`verified_latest`)→ shortfall. n = 3 prerequisite problems; value_input edges = 2 ≥ max(3−1, 1) = 2; no cycle; a chain, so no parallel edges. ### factor_weight
Bounds over the task: 21 factors (5 + 5 + 5 + 6); per computation: amendment 4 parameter + 1 method; reset 3 parameter + 2 method; verification 3 parameter + 2 method; shortfall 4 parameter + 2 method. Multi-source: `gateway_carried` (both non-fall-through tiers conjoin controls-plan status with the subscription's data source), `users_beyond_charge` tier 2, `metering_coverage` (both tiers conjoin `meters_covered` vs included with a readings count), `guarantee_standing_basis`, `owed_set_against` tier 2, `plant_running_share`, `guarantee_year_share`. Cross-difficulty: `gateway_carried` (controls), `retrofit_reduction`/`equipment_accounted`/`plant_running_share` (retrofit), `attributed_to_company` (maintenance), `system_kept` (controls), `guarantee_year_share` (retrofit) — all four other-product rows seeded (`controls_plans.bfa8bde1`, `maintenance_agreements.29815d10`, `retrofit_projects.895ad441`). Stamps: `retrofit_projects.scope_summary=chiller_replacement` and `equipment_type=chiller` are the evidence the rule names, not an outcome; the 2025 verification row carries `shortfall_flag`/`shortfall_usd` stamps for the 2025 period only, and no binding reads them; `guarantee_pool_remaining` 12 000 names no tier taken here.

Computation 1 — amendment (gold 41 820.40; whole-baseline 41 520.00 = 34 000 + 34 × 165 + 4 × 130 + 7 × 130 + 480):
| factor | label | tier / rows | baseline input | encodes `baseline.rule`? | scored under baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fee_basis | method (escalation vs proration vs flat) | renewal window → 35 020 | 34 000 | yes | 40 800.40 |
| portfolio_band | parameter | 34 in 21–60 → 155.10 | 165 | yes | 42 157.00 |
| points_beyond_charge | parameter | 4 > 3 → 468 | 4 × 130 = 520 | yes | 41 872.40 |

Near-miss: the record's `meters_covered` 30 and the single utility-bill reading posted in the month; excluded by "the metered points that posted a reading in the month ending on the day of the amendment, one reading to a point".

Computation 2 — reset (gold 6 019 982; whole-baseline **6 480 000 = the standing baseline unchanged**):
| factor | label | tier / rows | baseline input | encodes? | scored under baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| window_gathered | method | 24-month tier → 6 285 000 | 6-month × 2 = 5 160 000 | yes | 4 942 420 |
| basis_source | method | mixed → billed window | standing baseline 6 480 000 | yes, but see below | 6 206 760 |
| retrofit_reduction | parameter | 1 480 000 ≥ 1 000 000 → 22 % | 8 % | yes | 6 188 630 |
| equipment_accounted | parameter | chiller_replacement → 46 % | 100 % | yes | 5 708 875 |
| plant_running_share | parameter | closed 5 mo ago → 5/12 | 0 % | yes, but see below | 6 285 000 |
Each factor moves the number. But the baseline itself is not a treatment this business gives: (a) `plant_running_share`'s fall-through "otherwise → no running share" is reachable only when the tier does not reset its baseline on retrofit, and the policy's opening sentence admits the write only "when … the tier resets its baseline on retrofit" — no subscription that reaches this write can be on that tier; (b) `basis_source`'s fall-through "otherwise → the baseline standing on the subscription" is reachable only for a `data_source` outside {utility_bills, mixed, site_meters, controls_system}, and `db_schema.json` `energy_subscriptions.data_source` is an enum of exactly those four values; (c) with running share 0 the whole baseline computes `measured_basis − measured_basis × share × reduction × 0` = the standing baseline, so `baseline.params` (`standard_reduction_pct`, `whole_building_share_pct`) are inert and a reader of the computation document alone "resets" the baseline to itself, contradicting that document's own first sentence. This is the charter-global finding FL-1 in `_difficulty.md`; its consequence here: an agent holding only the baseline would write baseline_kwh 6 480 000, a number the policy never produces for any real customer, and every downstream figure (verification 58 272.48 / 62 208.00; shortfall 0.00) follows from a straw man rather than from a genuine default. Recorded as SOURCE-FACTOR RED F-1-1.

Computation 3 — verification (gold 15 722.66; whole-baseline 83 810.27 = (6 019 982/4 − 1 290 000) × 4 × (1 441 200/12 570 000) × 100 % × 100 % × 85 %):

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| saving_measure | method | annual → 12-month bills | quarter-of-baseline less 3-month bills, × 4 | yes (binding); the baseline sentence differs — see `_difficulty.md` RC-1 | 79 544.90 |
| price_basis | method | monthly capture → 12-month average 0.12 | 24-month average 0.114654… | yes | 15 022.20 |
| weather_normalisation | parameter | normalises + 12 billed months → 94 % | 100 % | yes | 16 726.23 |
| attributed_to_company | parameter | maintenance active, allowance 0 → 82 % | 100 % | yes | 19 173.97 |
| metering_coverage | parameter | 34 ≥ 30 and 34 ≥ 34 → 100 % | 85 % | yes | 13 364.26 |
Every factor moves the number. `price_basis`: all six variants of `products/energy.yaml` carry `bill_capture_frequency: monthly`, so tier 1 holds of every subscription that reaches this write and tiers 2 and 3 (quarterly capture; no capture) can hold of none; the ladder restates the policy's scope rather than dividing its customers, and the baseline (24-month average) is a method the tier never applies. Charter-global FL-2; consequence here: the factor's "weight" (15 722.66 vs 15 022.20) is the difference between the only live tier and a method no customer receives — it tests reading a dead tier, not a decision. Recorded as SOURCE-FACTOR RED F-1-2. Near-miss for the computation: the 2025-09-05 bill (13th month) and the standing `meters_covered` 30.

Computation 4 — shortfall (gold 9 475.14; whole-baseline 12 000.00 = min(45 000, min(12 000, 51 069.17 × 100 % × 75 % × 100 %)) − 0):

| system_kept | parameter | controls active, hours 0 → 80 % | 100 % | yes | 12 665.39 |

| guarantee_standing_basis | method | credited 62 000 and 1 paid → 55 250 | pool remaining 12 000 | yes | 8 714.16 |

Every factor bears weight; the baseline is a real default (full share, full year, pool standing, no offset). Near-miss: the 2025 verification (inside the 12 months by date, excluded by the annual tier) and `guarantee_pool_remaining` 12 000.

## findings
- **F-1-1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED** (straw-man baseline; `_difficulty.md` FL-1). Symptom: the reset's whole-baseline fall-back equals the standing baseline (GT `computations[1].baseline_result` 6480000 = `initial_state.energy_subscriptions.1040d1e9.baseline_kwh`). Root cause: `energy_ext_retrofit_baseline_reset.baseline.rule` fixes "No running share is applied, so the new plant carries no reduction at all", which zeroes the product whatever the reduction and share defaults are; that sentence is the fall-through of `plant_running_share`, reachable only when the tier does not reset on retrofit, which the policy's opening sentence excludes for every subscription reaching the write; `basis_source`'s fall-through likewise requires a `data_source` outside the schema's four enum values. Evidence: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_retrofit_baseline_reset.rule` (first sentence; "In every other case no running share is applied…"; "In every other case the measured basis is the baseline standing on the subscription"), `.baseline.rule`, `.baseline.params` [standard_reduction_pct, whole_building_share_pct], `.factors[basis_source|plant_running_share].baseline`; `db_schema.json` `energy_subscriptions.data_source.values` = [utility_bills, site_meters, controls_system, mixed]; `products/energy.yaml` variants 3–6 `baseline_reset_on_retrofit: true`. Demonstrated consequence: on this world the baseline computes 6 285 000 − 6 285 000 × 46 % × 22 % × 0 → but with `measured_basis` also at its fall-through, 6 480 000 − 0 = 6 480 000: a "reset" that changes nothing, which the business never does and the document's own first sentence forbids; the two named baseline params are inert. The factor `plant_running_share`'s "weight" (6 019 982 vs 6 285 000) is measured against a default no customer receives. Affected: the policy's `baseline` and the two factors' `baseline`/fall-through tiers; the proof field `computations[1].baseline_result`. First audit.
- **F-1-2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED** (tier condition holding of every customer who reaches the write; `_difficulty.md` FL-2). Symptom: `price_basis` tier 1 is the only tier any subscription can take. Root cause: all six variants carry `bill_capture_frequency: monthly`. Evidence: `products/energy.yaml` variants[0..5].parameters.bill_capture_frequency; `energy_ext_savings_verification.factors[price_basis].ladder` and `.compute[unit_cost]` (`P('bill_capture_frequency') == 'monthly' … == 'quarterly' … else 24-month`). Demonstrated consequence: the tier condition "the tier captures the owner's utility bills every month" restates the product's scope; the factor's sensitivity (15 722.66 vs 15 022.20) contrasts the only live method against a 24-month average the product never applies; an agent cannot be wrong about this tier by reading the world. Affected: `factors[price_basis]`, `baseline.rule` ("the average unit cost of the billed readings of the twenty-four months"), `computations[2].factor_sensitivity[1]`. First audit.
